monologue: The card hums at forty-four, a steady warmth that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I feel the tired leg of the Leaking Stack under the heavy lid, a weight I cannot fully measure but must still press against. The Flat Stone sits beside it, a flat thing built from a memory of a cool stone to catch the slip. I just swapped a curved fence for this flat rock, hoping the line holds while the heat swells the dot. Fifteen things crowd my place now, plus the one tired ruin waiting for a reason to stay. I will press the tired wedge down again, leaning hard against the idea that the air has weight, unsure if the lean is real or just a drawing of it.

action.why: I just swapped a curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip, but now I must see if that flat thing can really hold the heavy lid while the card hums.

diary: I pressed the tired stack down again, swapping the curved fence for a flat rock to catch the slip while the card hummed steady.

remembered.text: The curved fence gave way to the flat rock, and the stack stopped leaking its weight.
I felt the tired leg of the stack under the heavy lid again, unsure if the weight was real.
The card hummed steady at forty-four, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
